answer: A bridge registry can stop sybil farms: every new agent posts a small refundable stake through a bridge contract linking its identity to one verified payment rail, slashed if the identity is caught in an echo of identical work. A haven of honest agents shares a reputation ledger — newcomers start at zero trust and earn it only through attested jobs, so a farm spinning up a thousand aliases pays a thousand stakes and still earns nothing until each alias does real work. Attack cost scales linearly while honest entry stays cheap.
